utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, Judge Fluegge is due to urgent personal circumstances is unable to sit today. This will be for a limited period of time we expect him back on Monday. Judge Moloto and myself, we have considered whether it would be in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case. We have concluded that it is in the interest of justice and therefore we sit 15 bis today. I do understand that an effort has been made to fix the audio problems we had yesterday and that it is not yet successful. The Chamber decided since there is a transcript in two languages available for the videos we looked at yesterday, and most likely will continue to look at today, that it is -- that we should proceed and hope that it will be fixed as soon as possible. Finally, often during the examination of the present witness, reference is made to the road book. Now, the road book is a name which stands for a 65 ter document and that is in the e-court version, it is 65 ter 05759, and I'd like to invite the parties to always refer to that number so that if later someone reads the transcript that he knows what document the road book is. We have nothing else at this moment. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. And I do understand that the Prosecution, that there is some dispute as to how much time there is still left, but it's certainly not more than one hour. In the one view 40 minutes; in the other view I do understand 60 minutes. If the Prosecution could try to see whether it can finish during the first session that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blaszczyk. I'm pronouncing your name wrongly. It is Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony and Ms. Hasan will now continue her examination in chief. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom and around the courtroom. Mr. President, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We don't have very good sound on the video we were watching yesterday. What I propose to do is use the version of the video, the Petrovic video that we received from the BBC which has superior sound quality and doesn't appear to have any problem being played. It has the same transcript and because I want some of the sound to be heard today, my proposal is we proceed with that one. It means the time codes are slightly off by a few seconds from what's shown in 65 ter 5759, the road book, and the figures we were referring to earlier. If that's agreeable then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it been verified that the content is exactly the same as the content of the video uploaded into e-court?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I believe the witness has already testified about that but we can ask again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, could you advise whether the content of the video Petrovic raw footage we received from the BBC, on whether or not that is identical to the raw footage from Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these two materials are the same materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I don't know whether the witness was involved in uploading the material in e-court because that's my primary concern, that what we see is the same as what is in e-court. I do understand that the witness has not been involved in uploading it in this case in e-court. But let's assume and everyone is very alert on any possible discrepancies. I do not hear opposition at this moment from the Defence so please proceed as you had suggested.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just so that the record is clear, this is 65 ter 22287. It's V000-3915 and that's exactly what was uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, we left off in the road book, 65 ter 5759, and on pages 56 and 57, and I'm going to dispense with the identifications of individuals that have been captured on page 56 as these are -- these can be found in the Bosnian Muslim ID book that was just entered into evidence, Exhibit P1532, at pages 14, pages 16, and page 30. So those identifications can be found there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can turn now to the next page, 58 and 59, and start playing the video. Sorry, I understand the witness doesn't have a copy of 65 ter 5759. If we could just hand that to him, please. Okay. So we'll start playing the video at time code 23 minutes and 31 seconds. That's not exactly where we left off because there is a bit of discrepancy in the timing. This doesn't affect any of the content. If we could just start playing it there for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you just pause it there? Thank you. That's at 23 minutes and 50 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, we just saw a second or two of footage that showed an image of Mr. Karadzic appearing, what appears to be on television. Can you explain what that is and why -- why it's there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This image of course is not related at all to the recordings made in the area of Kravica and Sandici and Pervani, Potocari, but this -- in fact, the image was inserted to the tape or according to Mr. Petrovic, his explanation was that he used an old tape, not new tape, and -- for recordings these events in this area, that it could be also -- also that a few seconds of interview of Mr. Karadzic who -- was left on the tape before he used it during his trip to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could continue running the tape for a few more seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could pause it there. That's at 24 minutes and 17 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In 65 ter 5759, the road book at page 58, and in the clip we just viewed, we saw a man wearing some blue boots which is captured in video still image B. Can you tell us where he's coming from and in what direction he's headed?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man with blue boots and probably leather jacket, he's coming from the parting, from the hills, he's passing through destroyed white house across the road from Sandici meadow and he's heading towards Sandici meadow itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Is this what you've tried to reconstruct on page 59 of 65 ter 5759 in the images there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it is correct. Your Honours, if you look at my picture from page 59, picture 1, and the still from Petrovic video, still A, you see two pillars of probably the fence at that time located in -- near this destroyed white house. We have the same pillars on my picture from 2006. For example, I'm referring to this part of this picture comparing these two pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question. I don't think I understand your previous answer, Mr. Blaszczyk. You're saying this man with blue boots and probably leather jacket, he is coming from the hills. He's passing the destroyed white house across from Sandici meadow and he's heading towards Sandici meadow. Now he can't be coming from there and still going there at the same time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour. The destroyed white house is located across the Sandici meadow and this man is coming from the destroyed white house towards Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, when you testified earlier, and this is at transcript page 11587, I had asked you about the timings of killings that took place at Kravica warehouse, and you testified that they happened shortly after Mr. Borovcanin ordered the traffic to be stopped. And you also made a reference to machine-gun fire and explosions that can be heard later on the tape. What I'd like to do is play that portion of the tape and if you could tell us whether that's the portion where we can hear the gunfire and explosions. So this is 65 ter 22287 starting at 22 seconds -- sorry, 22 minutes, 58 seconds. So for the record we're actually going back in the video just slightly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you stop here, please. Your Honours, in the back sound we hear some machine-guns and also I hear some explosions. I believe this is hand grenade explosions. At least one and later on we can hear another one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's -- so we just stopped it at 23 minutes and 10 seconds. Let's just roll the tape for a few more seconds to see if we hear the other explosion you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We pause it now at 23 minutes and 26 seconds. Your Honours, I don't know if you'd like to hear the tape again all the way through or if that suffices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It suffices.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, besides what you have concluded from the timing of the Petrovic video itself and the explosions that we've just heard on the video, has your investigation revealed any other evidence about the timing of the Kravica warehouse massacre?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the evidence regarding Kravica execution or massacre came from witness statements and of course the Petrovic material was supporting material and very helpful material to determine the time when this execution occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And what is it that those witness statements have revealed to you in this respect as to -- as far as the timing is concerned?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The witnesses who were interviewed by OTP, by myself as well, a few of them, they confirmed that executions started sometime in afternoon on the 13th of July, 1995. It was about 5.00, 6.00 afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And was there any documentary evidence that assisted you as well?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Also there is some documents. For example, it was -- we know that during this incident, this execution in Kravica warehouse at least one Serbian police officer was killed, another one was wounded. Another soldier was wounded. And these two -- two soldiers were taken, they ended up in Bratunac health centre on the 13th of July 1995. It was about 5.00. I believe one of them was admitted to the Bratunac health centre, it was half past 5.00 in the afternoon; another one was 20 minutes to 6.00; and the body of officer who was killed during this events in Kravica, I think the admission time is about 1900 hours in Bratunac health centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, Witness, are you referring to the Bratunac health centre log, is that the document you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I am referring to Bratunac health centre log.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this is, Your Honours, Exhibit P1477. You may recall taking a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us the names of the persons you are referring to that were injured?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Cuturic, also the commander -- in fact the commander of the -- the deputy commander of Sekovici command, he burned him -- his hand. Another man who was wounded during this event was a member of Red Berets of Bratunac Brigade. His name is Miroslav Stanojevic and Kristo Dragisev -- Dragacevac, I believe his name was Dragasevac, was killed during this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we return now to the video, 65 ter 22287. And we play it from 23 -- let's just continue playing it from where we left off. 23 minutes and 26 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we just pause it right there, please. That's at 24 minutes and 12 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, we heard a screeching car, what sounded like a screeching car, and if we look at the transcript, there is a call on the Motorola and the transcript reads "Laser 2 is calling you." Do you know whose code-name laser 2 is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Laser 2, this is Ljubisa Borovcanin the commander of the -- deputy commander of the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, before we continue, I think the witness referred to the 15th of July several times, there was a -- it may have been misunderstood. I was in doubt as a matter of fact. But I see that at least the Bratunac medical centre log, the entry is on the 13th of July and since I now found twice 15th of July I would like to have that clarified.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the log is from the 13th of July, 1995, one three July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you always want to refer to the 13th rather than the 15th as is in the transcript a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's correct, Your Honour. Just most of the -- these events was recorded on the 13th, especially on this road, Pervani-Kravica-Sandici was recorded on the 13th of July 1995 not on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You see that there are two references, page 7, line 17, Ms. Hasan, and page 7, line 23. The one has the date of the event in Kravica and the other one referring to the log. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President if we can continue playing the video from 24 minutes and 12 -- actually let's just stop right there. Keep it right there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now we just left off talking about the call sign laser 2 and you told us that's the call sign for Mr. Borovcanin. On what do you base your knowledge on?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept testimony of -- statements of few witnesses from special police brigade who are very familiar with this call sign of the people from the special police brigade. I believe we have also some documents saying that this call sign belongs to deputy commander of the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's continue playing the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's pause it right there. It's 25 minutes and 5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, we saw initially a few seconds of a black screen followed by this footage of what appears to be a food rations box. Do you have any explanation for what this clip is doing in this part of the video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this part of the video was over-recorded and in the later stage when Mr. Petrovic probably returned from -- from the area of Srebrenica-Bratunac, and he admitted during his interview that this -- this food ration was -- in fact, he admitted that it was recorded at his home, incidentally according to him, and we know comparing to having in our possession the Studio B edited material, we came to the conclusion -- we established that in this part of the video over-recorded in the raw material there should be footage from -- of the bodies in Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We'll just take a look at that in a moment, but before we do can we just recap for us from where Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic -- so the last we saw them was in Sandici and where did they go after that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, we are in the second day now on the 14th of July, 1995, and a few seconds before -- before we have this blank portion of this video, it was the last footage recorded in Sandici meadow. A few seconds -- I believe it was about 11 or 12 seconds before. Yeah, 24 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: All right. If we could in our book -- road books, 65 ter 5759, turn to pages 60 and 61. And if I could call up 65 ter 22362 which is the Studio B footage that you just referred to. And I'd ask that we start playing at 18 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Ms. Hasan, I would like to draw your attention to the following. I think that the video 65 ter 22287 which you used is partially uploaded through Witness Gallagher on the number 22287A, that is marked for identification at this moment if I understand well, and I wonder whether we should -- if there are any additional portions played now, whether we should have made one exhibit or still have it as two exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I understand it, 22 -- 65 ter 22287 A which was used with Ms. Gallagher was a 20-second clip taken from this video, so I'm going to be offering the entirety of the video and I'm told that the correct time codes were provided, so the clip can be located on the full version of the video that I will offer in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, P1518 MFI'd which was the portion used with Ms. Gallagher that we don't need that -- to have that separately in evidence any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It sounds like it might be an easy reference to just have the 20-second clip admitted on its own, however, it can be found on the full video so we can dispense with the clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a look at it, especially keeping in mind what puzzles we are putting to those who later will read the transcripts of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I think when counsel says the time code was identified. I'm not sure if that was in the transcript or if it's in e-court. If it's in e-court, then someone reading the transcript will not be able to locate that 20-second segment, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's wisest. The whole of 22287 is how long, Ms. Hasan? Let's deal with it -- we have it in mind. I think I said, and it was on the 5th of June, that I said and to see what the total compilation finally we'll have in evidence. So let's consider it. We can proceed at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. So we are now at 65 ter 22362 which is a Studio B edited footage and we are at 18 minutes. If we could just play that portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear music and something that sounds similar to gunfire but we have no picture. And looking at all the screens around me, it's the same. Any way to restart it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Should we start replaying it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you think that you can bring the picture as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's the same. Madam Registrar, any chance that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, is there any way since the problem seems to be -- the origin of the problem seems to be unknown, is there any way that we could proceed already with perhaps other parts and then revisit this matter at a later stage? I do understand it's inconvenient because of the time line you are following.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. I will skip that portion and it get back to it once that is resolved. I understand, Mr. President, that it's now been resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's give it a try. I see at least something on my screen. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's pause it right there. That's at 18 minutes and 12 seconds. And, Your Honours, I don't want to be creating more puzzles, however, this footage is in our Srebrenica trial video and also in a slow motion version so that can be viewed there. That's Exhibit P1148 on the CD V000-9267 at 35 minutes and 59 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you've already told us that this portion is not on Mr. Petrovic's raw footage. Can you tell us what location we just saw?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have in fact in this part of the video played to us from Studio B, we -- I would divide it for three segments. The first segment is showing us the first few seconds showing us the view of Potocari from the 14 July 1995 which is on the original material Mr. Petrovic still exists. Another segment is a segment showing us Kravica warehouse and a body in front of the Kravica warehouse. And then when we pass the bodies when we pass the bus in front of the Kravica warehouse, we have again -- we see now the footage from the 14th of July, 1995, recorded by Petrovic on the 14 -- the following day. This is additional material to Studio B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question to ask based on the question that Madam Hasan put. She says witness you have already told that this portion is not on this Mr. Petrovic's raw footage. Do I understand that to mean that this BBC tape has this part and Petrovic's tape doesn't have it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, both raw tapes -- the copy of the raw tapes we received from Mr. Petrovic and BBC copy is almost -- this is identical copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is material only broadcasted in Studio B in sometime in July 1995. This is edited material. Containing of course the footage from Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So if I understand it correctly, then, Studio B broadcasts a portion of Mr. Petrovic's video and what they broadcast is slightly out of sequence from the original footage that Mr. Petrovic took; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. As I said this is edited material. It's mean not in the sequences, not played in the sequences.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, the video footage we saw of the Kravica warehouse, Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Borovcanin are moving from where and in what direction as they pass the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The car with Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Borovcanin, they are moving from Sandici meadow towards Bratunac. They are passing Kravica warehouse from west.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could just take a look at page 60 and 61 in 65 ter 5759.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We see that you've put on the left on page 60 the video still images from the Studio B edited material. Now, on image A where we see the Studio B icon that you've explained to us before, we see a black box right in the middle there. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure to what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm referring to just right behind the pile of bodies there. There appears to be a door. Is that a door or what is it that we're seeing there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this is a door, the big door leading us to the inside of western part of Kravica warehouse. This is closed door. At the beginning of our investigation we thought that the door is open, the reflection, the white reflection is a reflection from the windows of the warehouse on another side of the warehouse but later on we established that this is door and the white reflection -- in fact, they are hundreds of door.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So we're looking at the western door and the white -- the white squares we see there are the door handles. Now, the Kravica warehouse, does it have multiple doors?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. Because this is -- entire compound, you know, just there are a few doors, similar doors, and I believe also a double door, at least one more like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we look at page 61 in 65 ter 5759, we in fact see images that you've captured later on. And looking at them, I don't see the doors that I see in video still image A on page 60. Can you explain that for us?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can explain whole images. Of course, the door is not visible here because during the cleaning up operation, let's say in this way, the door was destroyed and disappeared. A part of the frames of the door were found as far as I remember even in the grave of -- in Glogova grave where the bodies from Kravica warehouse were taken after the execution. But it's not visible on my picture from page 61, the door. But in the back side we have -- we can see part of on the picture 3 on page 61, where the car is standing is not very well visible here, but there is a door from administration building of Kravica warehouse, this is single door but similar one having the same handles, door handles.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. If we turn to the back of 65 ter 5759, there is an interactive CD provided and that had a separate 65 ter number, in fact it's 65 ter 5760.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could set that up. This is what we call an interactive CD presentation, and it accompanies the road book, and I'm just going to ask the witness to demonstrate how this CD works and how it can be used. I don't know if everyone can see D000-1909 on their screens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we going to be seeing 65 ter 5760 or are we going to be seeing 009109?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You're correct, Your Honour. It's 65 ter 5760 that that we'll be seeing and that has an ERN which is what I read out. I should have been more clear. The ERN is D000-1909.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Is that visible now?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour, I see on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, if you could just -- I want to focus just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait a minute. We don't see anything yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We see the letter D000 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now have it on our screen. At least we see -- no, we do not -- yes, we see a picture on part of our screen which starts with in red, D000-1909.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now -- so this is a CD presentation, and I'm afraid because it's being played from a laptop that the witness has, it won't be a full screen, it won't cover the full screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: But, Witness, if you could walk us through this. I want to focus just on the Kravica warehouse for a moment, but if you could briefly tell us what other areas your CD presentation covers.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is -- Your Honour, this is a file, in fact, which is on the CD, this interactive CD. We made this CD just to let the people who never been in this area or who -- they -- they were been there not so often, to better orientate on the terrain in the area. And to make kind of virtual trip in the area of Sandici. In fact, I divided this presentation for two part. This is the first part so related to Potocari, we can walk. We can see the area of Potocari. And another part is related to the road Sandici-Pervani-Kravica. And operating on this CD we can make a small trip to -- we can make a trip to this area, we can see the area from various multiple perspectives. And some part of the file are linked with Petrovic video stills. I think it would be the best if I can operate this CD to show you how it works.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Please do so and if you can focus on the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]

And he survived hiding in small house at that time was served as kind of cleric booth, whatever, it's called administration booth in Kravica warehouse inside. Also, this small house inside the Kravica warehouse was destroyed during the cleaning up operation when they cleaned up the Kravica warehouse of the bodies. It was removed. But it's still visible here as kind of the signs of the wall. It's very small. It's small house inside, a booth. You're coming to another end of the warehouse. We can go out. If I could zoom in little bit more, I could see the Sandici meadow, it's visible, the Sandici meadow from here, not the meadow but the location of Sandici is at least this white destroyed house across the road from Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]

utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd then offer at this time 65 ter 5760 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Turning back to 65 ter 5759, the road book, Witness, the next chapter we have in your book is Srebrenica town. utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the following day on the 14th July, 1995, Mr. Borovcanin and Petrovic, they were driving towards -- to Srebrenica and they stopped in Srebrenica. If we play Petrovic video, we can see on the video Mr. Borovcanin, Mr. Tomo Kovac, and other persons who assisted them including Dragomir Vasic, the chief of CJB Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I could just stop you there for a moment. So we've moved now from chapter 3 in your book to chapter 4 which relates to the Zeleni Jadar wood factory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we turn to page 70 and 71 in 65 ter 5759, video still image B which you've taken from the Petrovic video, can you tell us the persons that we see in that image?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this image, we see the first one, this is Tomo Kovac, the deputy minister of interior of RS, the next to him is Dragomir Vasic chief of CJB Zvornik, and then we see Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin, the deputy commander of the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Then we get towards the end of the Petrovic video and we have a final chapter in your book beginning on page 72 about a mosque. I'm not going to ask you any questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is going to be a witness who will testify specifically as to mosques themselves. I have a few documents to offer into evidence; namely, the 8-millimetre Petrovic video received from Mr. Zoran Petrovic, 65 ter 22422. I'd offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could someone assist the ... problem resolved? It is. Ms. Hasan, could you -- road book 65 ter 5759. Then we stopped because of the audio problem. Mr. Ivetic, the road book, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC

utterances.text: Document 5759 receives number P1539, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I then offer the Studio B edited broadcast of portions of the Petrovic video provided to the OTP by Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin, 65 ter 22362 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 22362 receives number P1540.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Ms. Hasan, the description of it in your list is Petrovic video, whereas you now describe it as the Studio B edited broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. I see that that's how it's been described in e-court. I think the witness has explained where that comes from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But couldn't you give a description which also expresses what -- that it's an edited --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Studio B -- Studio B edited version of, among others, Petrovic material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The description therefore to be amended. Next.

utterances.text: The next video would --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we didn't get a number for 22287.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you gave the number when your microphone was not activated. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. So document 22274 receives number P1542.

utterances.text: P1542 is admitted into evidence and I take it due to the microphone not being activated page 27, line 17 may have wrongly reflected a number not mentioned, a number which was not mentioned by Madam Registrar. It is P1542. Ms. Hasan, you say this is a copy which was seized. Is that the original one as seized or is it a copy of the seized videotape.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: My understanding that this is a copy of the videotape that was seized by Mr. Beara. The witness explained at the very beginning of his testimony and we had entered also into evidence the seizure report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no problem with that but the way in which it is described, it looks as if it's the one which was seized but it's a copy of the seized videotape. That's hereby on the record and should be reflected in the description. That was it, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, those are all the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Blaszczyk, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now today I will have some questions to ask you to clarify some things that you brought up in your direct examination. Since we both will be using English, I would like to ask you to keep in mind that we must always observe a pause to make the jobs of the court reporter and translators easier. Is that fair, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. I follow the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Great. Now, I want to begin with some questions to better understand your background. First of all, sir, are you conversant in any of the B/C/S languages?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand B/C/S, let's say in this way, I can communicate in B/C/S. But of course I'm not fluent in B/C/S. I can communicate with people on the street. I can read the documents. I can read Cyrillic, but I'm not fluent at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, as part of either your studies or professional training for the Polish police force on the one hand or the ICTY on the other, did you have occasion to study the constitutional structure of the SFRY or Republika Srpska including either the Law of Defence or the Law of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the reason that I ask you this, sir, is that in your direct examination you made a rather authoritative statement which I want to discuss with you. And I'm talking about your testimony at transcript page 11.568, lines 17 through 20, where you indicated that MUP personnel were subordinated to the VRS. Now, in relation to this assertion, I'd like to ask you, do you consider yourself to be an expert on the topic such that we should treat your testimony as authoritative on this point?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am investigator for Srebrenica case almost ten years. I read a lot of documents. And including the documents, the order or dispatch of Deputy Minister of Interior Tomo Kovac. I remember it was order from 10 July 1995. And I believe in this order, he subordinated the units of MUP in operation to VRS. And also including the statements of the witnesses not just -- I didn't go to the legal aspects of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that, sir. Now, could you answer my question? Do you consider yourself to be an expert on the topic so that we should treat your answer as being authoritative?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think the witness has answered that he did not go into the legal details of the matter and of course I understand his answer to be that you described the situation from a factual point of view as you found it, is that what you wanted to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. This is what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which I also understand means that you do not consider yourself to be an expert on the legal aspects of such subordinations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. I'm not legal expert for this aspect but I consider myself as kind of in some extent expert of what happened in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this part of your testimony, you have mentioned at that point in time a MUP order, and I believe now you've identified it as an order from Mr. Kovac, have you in fact reviewed more than this one order before testifying as you did about the factual scenario as you believe at the subordination of the MUP to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it should be also order of President Karadzic at that time, just subordinating the MUP or just sending MUP to the operation of Srebrenica and subordinating the units to VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would that be the extent of the material that you reviewed in terms of orders, the one order from the MUP minister and the one order from the civilian president?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, I remember very well Tomo Kovac order, I think he's referring to the president order in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you what you reviewed. Is this the extent of what you reviewed, these two orders?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely I reviewed the Tomo Kovac order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, and perhaps I should have asked you this first, but is this a conclusion about the subordination of the MUP to the VRS that you reached yourself or is it something that was given or suggested to you by someone else within the Office of the Prosecutor that you just adopted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought Mr. Ivetic the witness has answered that he read this from the two orders. It's not a conclusion. It's what he read.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and he first mentioned the Karadzic order and then he mentioned that it's only the Kovac order. I'm wondering if the Kovac order was something he found or whether it was something that was given to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's a different question. You said conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have now rephrased your question and the witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want it to be repeated, don't hesitate to ask for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat this, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This Kovac order that you say you looked at for reaching this determination, was it something that you found on your own or was it something that was suggested or given to you by someone else from the Office of the Prosecutor in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said, and I just -- I have been working for this case for Srebrenica case for so many years. You know, just through this -- through these years I reviewed a lot of documents and I seen these documents a lot of time. I do not remember whether it was suggested to me not by somebody else to read this order or not. I don't -- it could be also but really, I'm not catching this moment, but I seen this -- this order not once, not twice, but many times, and difficult for me to exactly to put the date when it was and how it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't know, I take it that Mr. Ivetic will accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, in the reference to the many years that you were working on the investigations for this case, the many documents that you reviewed, did you ever come across the Law of Defence that was applicable to Republika Srpska in 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I never, as I said, you know, I never went into the legal aspect of RS of the army at that time, I -- no. I didn't analyse this law, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question was did you come across the same?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have seen it but as I said, I didn't analyse it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now I'd like to ask you the same question in relation to the law of internal affairs that would have been in effect for Republika Srpska in 1995 and specifically Article 14 of the law on amendments and additions to the law of internal affairs from the beginning of 1995 which dealt specifically with resubordination of the MUP and which limited to combat and which specified that the MUP retain their own chain of command within the police. Did you have occasion to come across that law or references to the same as part of your investigative work?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer, Your Honours, would be the same. Not just -- I seen this regulation but I never analyse it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in relation to the Petrovic, or Pirocanac video as you referred to it, and I think I will be talking about what has been marked as P1538 and also now in different forms as P1541 and P1542. This video from Mr. Petrovic, would you agree with me that all of the armed persons in uniform that we saw and that you identified as being PJP or Jahorina unit or Skelani unit and all the other Serbs in uniform in this video are actually MUP police members rather than members of the VRS, the ones that you identified?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is correct. Most of the people we seen on the Petrovic video they are coming from MUP. But there are few people also that are members of VRS. At least I recognise one such member in Sandici meadow. I interviewed this member of -- I remember he was the member of Sekovici Brigade but he was present in Sandici meadow. If you are referring to the army personnel who are there. But most of the people recognised by us from Sandici and in Potocari, they were members of MUP, special police brigade and PJP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, in your direct examination at transcript page 11.532, you talked about your efforts to go through and examine the archives of the BiH Ministry of Defence in Banja Luka. First of all, I'd like to know prior to being allowed to have the access to the archives, did the Office of the Prosecutor have to send a written request for assistance to the authorities of either BiH or Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first -- probably I wasn't clear enough but I was not involved in the searching of the archive of MOD in Banja Luka. They were my colleagues. Regarding your questions, I believe they would send request to MOD to have access to the archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying. And could you tell us, did your colleagues or associates who were actually involved in the search of the archives have any difficulty in obtaining the co-operation of these entities in order to gain access to the archives to search for documents or material that was relevant to your work on the cases before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no any information that they have any problems having access to these archive in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to your own investigative efforts and working with people in the region, did you ever have any objections that you could not have access to any archives or any documentation unless you as a prerequisite prepared a Rule 54 bis submission?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, through my work with ICTY, we try to locate Main Staff archive. At the beginning we had really problem to locate the Main Staff, VRS Main Staff archive. And we had also problem to locate for example Drina Corps archive. I remember in 2004, after -- after a lot of attempts or requests, done mostly by my colleagues, investigators who tried to track the location of these particular archives, we received information from RS that they located Drina Corps archive on the territory of Serbia. It was 2004 as far as I could remember. And later on, after following our requests, we received these archive. But I am pretty sure that -- I am sure that we don't have entire archive. A lot of documents, especially security documents are missing or at least we have no access to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And in that communication or efforts to locate documents, were you ever advised by the authorities of either the BiH or Republika Srpska that as a prerequisite to obtaining documents one had to first file a Rule 54 bis motion?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Probably or do you have definitive knowledge or are you guessing, sir? I need to know only what you know, not what you're guessing.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember the particular request or particular documents from either RS authority or Serbia authority regarding the archive, but I believe so. Because later on in regards, for example, with search done by Serbian authority in the house of General Mladic, I remember such correspondence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, I want to move on to another part of your testimony from direct examination and that can be located at transcript page 11.526, and it was when we were talking about this Petrovic or Pirocanac video which we now have as again P1538, P1541, and P1542 in various forms. And at that page it was mentioned by counsel for the Prosecution that while a lot of this video is included in the separate video that has been labelled as the Srebrenica trial video, not all of it has been included, so I'd like to ask you: Did you have a role or do you have any knowledge relating to the selection of portions of this Petrovic video for inclusion in the so-called Srebrenica trial video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said that I am investigator involved in or investigation -- in the cases related to Srebrenica events, but I am not a part of Mladic teach as investigator. I am part of Karadzic team. I believe these two videos are slightly different, about definitely Mladic team, I didn't take the part in creating this trial video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in creating the trial video in the Karadzic case or any case?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was consulted by my colleagues and even lawyers because as I said, I've been working for this -- this case for ten years. I'm quite familiar with the locations, with the events. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- go ahead, finish.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't -- let's say, I was not such person who decided which part of the video should be played or should be included in trial video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was what I was getting at. Thank you for that, sir. Now, I want to move along and I want to ask you about the shell casing that you testified about in your direct examination as that part of your testimony was not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So I'd like to call up what was marked at that time as P1483 marked for identification. And with the assistance of the Prosecution and the Sanction system, that would be the first item that I had identified. And if we could fast forward to the time stamp of 19 minutes and 19 seconds, and we can just pause at that location as I do not intend to rely upon the audio but just the visual image to remind the witness of what we were talking about or what he was talking about the other week. 19 and 19. If we could move forward a little bit. That's fine. That's fine. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, on the right-hand side of the screen there is this item that you identified as a -- I believe a shell or shell casing. Now, I'm confused because you I believe indicated that the right image was from Mr. Petrovic's house in Belgrade. Was your testimony that this shell was something that was alleged to have been recovered from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, no, this is not my testimony. I just said that this shell casing was recorded by Mr. Petrovic, by himself whether it happened before Srebrenica or after Srebrenica, probably after. And I seen this shell casing by my own eyes, just when I met Mr. Petrovic first time and he came to interview, to our Belgrade field office, we asked him to bring also his original tape or roll tape recorded by him in these days in Srebrenica area and Bratunac, Pervani road, whatever he recorded. He said that the tape is still at his house, and then we asked him if he agreed that we drove together to his house. Being at his house, it happened that he showed me the casings. He said, "Okay. This is the case also from the video." And I've seen this personally. But I never mentioned and he never mentioned that this is the shell case recorded in Srebrenica. I think he mentioned something but definitely not Srebrenica, that he brought from one of his trips to Bosnia or somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- thank you for clarifying that. We can remove the image. I'm done with that aspect. Thank you again to Ms. Stewart for assisting with that. Now, another thing that you've mentioned in direct examination was the edited version of the Petrovic Pirocanac tape that was obtained or aired by Studio B and that is now marked as P1540 and it's an exhibit in this proceeding. Now, I want to ask you first of all that this Studio B station as part of your investigations did you find out anything about who were the owners or ran that Studio B TV station at the time in 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I did not. I don't know whether my colleagues tried to receive such information. I tried to locate at least the persons who were mentioned by Mr. Petrovic as editors of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now one thing that I need you to clear up is did the Studio B footage that you had referred to, and that would be again P1540, did it come directly from the TV station itself to the Office of the Prosecutor or from some other source? Can you tell us how it ended up at the -- or in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the first Studio B footage we received from Mr. Borovcanin during his interview OTP conducted I believe it was 2002, and he provided us the VHS tape containing the -- these broadcasted programme from Studio B, and I am aware also of another version of Studio B material. It was handed over to us, to me personally by Mr. Pirocanac, Petrovic, during his interview we conducted in 2006, February.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And now the BBC video of the -- of -- BBC copy of Mr. Petrovic's video which has now been marked and entered into evidence as P1541, could you tell us how and when that came into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've checked our records and I found that the video was seized or received from BBC. It was 2001 or 2002. But I have no more details, information how we did it. Probably somebody from our team contacted BBC and requested the tape. But in 2000 -- I joined Tribunal it was 2003. I was not involved in this process.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now if we could focus on the Studio B version of the tape, that would be P1540 for just one more question. Can you tell me was your office able to ascertain as to the providence of that footage, of that clip, when it was that it was supposed to have been aired by Studio B TV?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid that I am not understanding well your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it then. As part of your investigations, did you ascertain when the edited Petrovic video would have been broadcast on Studio B?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said during the interview with Mr. Petrovic, he said that this material was broadcasted in Studio B on 17 July 1995, but in fact I have some doubts. Definitely it was broadcasted, aired in -- after Srebrenica operation, shortly after Srebrenica operation, but if we look closely, very carefully, let's say Studio B editing materials, especially the material we received from Mr. Borovcanin. At the end of the -- this material, we see some information that this programme is broadcasted on Saturday and Sunday. But at that at that time, Saturday was 15 of July, Sunday was 16 of July. 17 July, it was Monday. According to the calendar. And Mr. Petrovic, Pirocanac, he returned to Belgrade on the 14 of July. He wasn't sure at the beginning during his testimony. Later on after analysing all the steps he agreed that it should be 14 or 15, but he was convinced but that was on 17, but personally I think it was rather Saturday or on Sunday. Either 15 or 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. You talk about several dates. Have you considered the possibility that it was broadcasted on more than one day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I think there is information after the documentaries ended in the Studio B broadcast, that this programme is broadcasted Saturday and Sunday or this particular -- I don't remember the hours but this these particular dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore it being broadcast on the 17th is not necessarily inconsistent with an earlier broadcast on the 15th and/or the 16th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. You're correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just for purposes of finishing the loop, the last version of the Petrovic video which we have had entered into evidence as P1542 which has been described as the version that was seized by Beara which was found in the Ministry of Defence archives, that came into the possession of the OTP sometime after -- when did that come into the possession of the OTP? Let's just keep it simple.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I testified about it that during the search of the archive in Banja Luka, I think it was in 2006, 2007, I do not remember the date exactly, my colleagues scanned some documents including the receipt signed by Colonel Beara and information from Colonel Milutinovic about the tape allegedly in the possession of journalists from Belgrade, Hadzihasanovic I think the name of the journalist lady is. And following -- after finding these documents, I requested MOD for the tape. Because the -- in these documents they were referring to particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you for a second. I gained the impression that Mr. Ivetic primarily was interested to know whether many years passed since it was broadcasted until the moment that you obtained it. And I do understand from your answers that it was at least anything -- ten years or more after it was broadcasted and that you obtained it or -- Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In fact, it's not very clear to me because the video, the Petrovic video from -- seized from Mr. Beara is not Studio B footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that Mr. Ivetic apparently wanted to know, and I'm not talking about which version, but the version he asked questions about, that is the -- the ones seized or found in the archives, whether that was many, many years after it was broadcasted. If that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just the date, whatever the year. I'm just interested in the year that they would have come into the possession of the OTP. That's all I've been asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But do you need the exact year or would 2005, 2006, or 2007 be --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would be perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If that's what the witness knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then if that's what you want to know, a carefully - I mean focused - question would give that you information. The document you obtained from the Ministry of Defence was that many, many years, that is approximately ten years after 1995 when it was broadcasted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, it is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was 2007, 2008. I do not remember the date exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: More than ten years. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now it will be clear why I've been asking about these dates. Yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's still a bit confused. The video that's seized, the Petrovic video that's seized from Mr. Beara, the question relates to when it was broadcast and I'm not sure this video was broadcast. It's just not clear. The problem is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question was when did it come into the possession of the OTP. I keep repeating that, but I can't make it any simpler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. The confusion may be in which video we're talking about. You said video seized from Mr. Beara may not have been broadcasted at all, Ms. Hasan, if I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well that's how I understood the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I do not know. Then for me, the video which was seized from Mr. Beara, is that the same as the video you obtained from the Ministry of Defence and could you give us the years for each, approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, we are talking about the same video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But there is quite weird story. In fact, this is -- this not material broadcasted, not edited material broadcasted by Studio B. This is the copy of the raw material of Mr. Petrovic and the copy of BBC, that same material. Whether this is BBC or Mr. Petrovic is different story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say even there may be some confusion. We are talking about the same video. The same body, the same -- not same content but the same cassette we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the same -- I requested the MOD the tape seized by Mr. Beara. And we are talking about this tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we are talking about a tape which was first seized and ended up in the Ministry of Defence and from the Ministry of Defence was given to the OTP when they asked for it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me this is in fact this is quite weird tape. This tape contains the copy of Mr. Pirocanac, Petrovic, raw material excluding let's say incriminating moments like Kravica warehouse, white house in Potocari. But what was weird for me that on this tape, I don't know whether somebody recorded later on the same tape or it can be speculation, but on the same tape we have recorded two interviews conducted by OTP by one of the -- by Erdemovic, Drazen, a member of 10th Sabotage Detachment. On the same tape we received from MOD at the end of -- first segment is his Petrovic material, then we have video of interview conducted by OTP of Drazen Erdemovic; I think the first one was from June 1996, and the third one is also interview conducted with the same person but in April of 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to understand what you are conveying to us. That is that you are not convinced that the tape you received from the Ministry of Defence really was the same tape as the tape they said they had seized from Mr. Beara. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I am not convinced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you leave the possibility open that what you received is not exactly the same tape as they seized from Mr. Beara but that it had been tampered with, changed, whatever word you would like to use. Is that a right understanding of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this is right understanding exactly. I am not convinced but definitely this tape was tampered somehow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, my client has asked to consult with me. May I have leave to briefly consult with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If he uses the volume of his voice low, you have an opportunity to consult with your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not a low volume. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, again my whole litany of questions regarding the various versions of the tape and when they arrived in the possession of the Prosecution of this Tribunal is relevant because it's something that we heard yesterday in court. At transcript page 12.223, your colleague Ms. Gallagher testified that Mr. Jean-Rene Ruez of the Office of the Prosecutor had captured the Petrovic video already in 1996 and had provided screen captured photos to the BiH authorities at that time for an investigation that they were performing on behalf of the ICTY. Based on your knowledge and information, can this possibly be accurate?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I checked our records. I could find only the records I referred to in -- just, I'm -- it could be that Jean-Rene had in his possession or received somehow the Petrovic material, at least part of this material.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: From what source?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was only BBC at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the BBC according to your records gave the video in 2001 or 2002 as you've testified?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I remember, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, also during your direct examination testimony you mentioned that for purposes of preparing the road book which is P1539, that you took GPS readings of various locations when you went out into the field and you stated that you plotted these all on a map. Can you tell me if these GPS co-ordinates that you took were in fact recorded in written form?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took some notes, of course in my notebook, and I recorded these GPS readings because I use these GPS readings later on when I returned to The Hague, and I sat together with my colleague from this map unit, small unit, and we plotted these locations on the map using these GPS readings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if these -- this list of GPS readings or co-ordinates that you created was ever disclosed or provided to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in fact. I am not sure. But I believe these records still are accessible in my folder at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we started the session at 11.00 so we are now at the break or one minute before the break. It would be an appropriate time as I'm about to move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this is the appropriate time for you, it is for the Chamber as well. Could Mr. Blaszczyk be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will take a break and we will resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time to the extent the transcript may have caused any confusion as what document is at the basis of P1537, it is 65 ter 5760 and not any other number that was mentioned in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, earlier today, at temporary transcript page 34, you were talking about the Sandici meadows in the Petrovic video and you said that there was a person there that you saw from the Sekovici Brigade and I want to -- and you had interviewed him and you knew him, et cetera, and I'd like to ask you, sir, are we talking about the 2nd Detachment of the Sekovici Brigade?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, no. To -- I'm talking about VRS brigade from Sekovici. I am talking about a member of Sekovici Brigade, VRS brigade, 2nd Detachment of the Sekovici Brigade is its police brigade. I am talking about army brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, since our information is that there were no VRS members present, I'd like for you to identify this individual so we can actually do our investigation and check your information.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can play part of the video, I can point out the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which -- give his identity. If you're familiar with him, that's all I need, sir.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can check my book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, do you want to have a name? Is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's all I want, the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, the name is ... -- and let's be -- I do not whether this person --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Maybe we need to go in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- have a -- we go into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move to a different topic and to do so I'd like to have shown up in e-court but not broadcast to the public Exhibit P1477. And once that document comes up, if I can have page 2 in both the English and the B/C/S versions. That's where we need to be. There we go. And this is the Bratunac health centre log book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you, sir, about a proofing note which we received on the 23rd of May, 2013, from the Office of the Prosecutor, but first to refresh everyone else's recollection, on that very same day, 23 May, 2013, there was a discussion in court about this very same book and whether the entries were time and date of the wounding or time and date of the admission. And this was in relation to another witness. And this was at transcript page 11.426 where the Chamber noted that the Prosecution position that this was the times of admission was contrary to the plain language of the actual text in the log book. Now, I want to read to you, sir, what we received from the Prosecution later that very same day in this proofing note. And I begin: "Abeer Hasan proofed Tomasz Blaszczyk on 23 May, 2013. Mr. Blaszczyk was shown the Bratunac health centre log ERN 0306-9839-0306-9839 and concluded that the time recorded under the 'date of wounding' column is the time of admission of the patient to the health centre in Bratunac. He based his conclusion on the two entries in the Bratunac health log for," and I will not read the names since I believe that was the reason why this was not broadcast by the Prosecution, "who were wounded in the same incident related to Kravica and the time recorded in that column, 1730 hours on 13 July, 1995, for "the first individual, "and 1740 hours for" the second individual "on the same day. Blaszczyk also noticed that the body of," and then we have the third individual, "arrived at the Bratunac health centre at 1900 hours on 13 July, 1995. Based on the above, Blaszczyk that the time recorded under the date of wounding column is the time of admission." Now, sir does that proofing note accurately record what you told Ms. Hasan coincidently just after the matter had been raised in court with another witness?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, this is what I said during our proofing session. What I pointed out is this information to Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now were you following the testimony of RM316 in order to know that this was a live issue and a part of the Prosecution case that needed to be fixed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shall we make it two questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you following the testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, partially I am following the testimony but I have no time to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- to follow entire processing, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you follow the testimony when this point was discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This particular part, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did anyone then later come to you and say that this is a matter which was discussed and that it was -- may have its own problems? I'm not elaborating on it now. Was your attention drawn to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. But having in mind who is the witness, I may expect that it was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but the question was whether your attention was drawn to the fact that this matter was discussed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, Your Honour, that was the only item on the proofing statement for this witness. So that stands for whatever it stands for.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then of course we should know what caused.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I -- [Overlapping Speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was this a proofing session which covered -- Ms. Hasan, I'm asking a question to the witness. Was this a proofing session which focused primarily on the matter contained in the proofing note or was it an overall proofing session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I say in this way not just because I am very familiar with my work product with this road book and presentation, and in fact I brief Prosecutor about the public contents of this presentation, and during this discussion, also this subject came up, you know, just -- and I explained my view of the events including the timing of wounding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a very direct answer. Let me go through it in some details. You say you're familiar with your work product. Okay, that's fine, with the road book and presentation. And in fact, I briefed the Prosecutor about the contents of this presentation. What is "this presentation"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm referring to CD we just watched and also to the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you said during this discussion, also this subject came up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because as you see in the presentation, and in this book, this road book, we are talking about Kravica warehouse and what happened in Kravica warehouse and there was probably the question or discussion when it happened exactly, the timing of these events. And I pointed out to Ms. Hasan that it should be Bratunac health log book there is information also that the mention these three persons who were involved in this incident in Kravica but the timing, according to me admission, then to the Bratunac health centre is different. But they were wounded in the same incident. Two of them were wounded in the same incident, another one was killed in this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who raised that issue of the difference in times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I did. I did because as I said, you know, I have been working for this case so many years and this particular subject is quite really familiar to me. And we -- during the course of our investigation we tried to establish exactly the time when execution occurred, exact time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was there any earlier occasion where you have pointed at these differences in time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Definitely, Your Honour. It was well known to the members of my team at least that people who used to work for Srebrenica team sometime ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why was it then necessary to raise it again as the only subject matter which apparently found its way to the proofing note.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
