utterances.text: I think this part, this information sounded quite new for Ms. Hasan and probably she decided to put in the proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did she tell you anything about the other witness and the issue raised with that other witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Ivetic. Ms. Hasan -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It seems there's been some sort of allegation of misconduct here, and if that's the case I'd like for us to be able to address it. We don't need to address it in front of this witness, but if that's the case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What happens, Mr. McCloskey, is there was -- some questions were put by Mr. Ivetic which triggered a need to carefully establish the facts which were apparently relevant for Mr. Ivetic and may be relevant for the Chamber as well. That's simply facts. I didn't ask for anything than facts, did I? As I usually try --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe there's some insinuation of some -- that there's something improper about Ms. Hasan's asking Mr. Blaszczyk about this subject --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- and that's apparently where he's going, and I don't see that there's anything improper about this. And if it's going to be gone into further, I would like for us to be able to discuss it. If that's not what's happening and I'm misreading this, I will sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me say the following: The line of questioning initiated by Mr. Ivetic required, in my view, and that's the reason why to some extent I took over, a careful consideration of facts, first of all, before you start thinking things Mr. Ivetic may have had on his mind but then not expressed. Mr. Ivetic, I think -- am I far wrong that it came to your mind at least for a second that there may have improper behaviour but that you also thought it important to know the facts before to further develop those thoughts?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, and also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did I assist new that respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You did assist me, Your Honour. And it also goes towards the reliability and credibility of this witness and the motives that he has to testify, and that's why I'm asking about the facts that he knows and has access to, and that's I believe -- that was the focus of my asking him and I have some additional questions in that regard that I think will be relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not dreaming this up. He used the word and suggested that this topic in this proofing note was a mere coincidence despite that it being the question of the earlier witness, and it was of course no mere coincidence and there's nothing wrong with it so he -- I know what he's suggesting. And he's suggesting some sort of impropriety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the knowledge that you say -- that either we've talked about, that you have about the log book and what the actual columns mean, did you at any point in time do any prior investigative work to ascertain or confirm your view of what the columns on the log book mean?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally not but I am aware that my colleagues did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in relation to your testimony about -- or your knowledge about the log book, you identify the first entry on the page, I will not say the name because, again, it's my understanding that we're not supposed to mention the names, and this individual is listed or identified as a Red Beret member, and I believe that you -- well -- I believe you mention that one member of the army was wound in this -- at this location in Kravica -- at Kravica warehouse. Am I correct that this unit with the designation of the Red Berets had in fact been disbanded as a unit of the Bratunac Brigade at some point in time prior to July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid that you are wrong. That unit was disbanded but after -- after events in July of 1995, and most of the people from these Red Berets unit the -- unit were deployed as MUP members to Srebrenica police station but after -- after -- I think it was sometime, if I could remember, 14 or 15 of July 1995. Until then, the unit was the part of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade and existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you gave rather specific information today at transcript page 8 of the temporary transcript about the log book or at least about the times when these individuals were admitted for treatment apart from looking at the log book, so I'd like to ask you if it -- first of all, is it correct that on 27 May 2013 after you took the oath to testify and after you were instructed not to have contact about your testimony that you received an e-mail from a fellow Prosecution investigator giving precisely the substance of the meaning of the times in this log book which you were advised to disregard by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I received an e-mail from my colleague, and later on I -- immediately after the e-mail I received a telephone from the Prosecutor advising me to disregard this e-mail and -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So what I need to know, sir, is did you receive the advice to disregard this e-mail in time or did you in fact read this e-mail that was sent to you after you had taken your oath?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to admit that I read this e-mail because I received the e-mail I just read this e-mail and yeah, I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me the substance of this e-mail from your fellow investigator is precisely the testimony as to when, what the meaning of the times on this log book we are looking at is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but in fact it -- you have surprised me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough I'm just trying to get the facts, sir. Now, I'd like to clarify them with you. At transcript page 11.587, lines 1 through 7, in talking about the killing of persons at the Kravica warehouse, you say that the killings were done by the Sekovici detachment of the police and probably one member of the army. And first of all I want to clarify with you now, the Sekovici detachment that you were talking about would be a MUP police unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am referring here to Sekovici detachment, I am referring to the Special Police Brigade Sekovici Detachment, this is MUP unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now apart from the one individual who was wounded that we've talked about that you said was a member of the Red Berets that you claim was an army personnel, can you tell us what is the basis of your assertion and testimony that probably one army soldier was present and participated in the killings at Kravica? What would be the basis of that testimony?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except -- except these records from the Bratunac health centre, you know, proving that one member of the army was present over there, that he was wounded during this incident, we are in possession also of statements of the witnesses who testified or were interviewed by the state court in Bosnia-Herzegovina. A few of them, they were members of the army in fact in Kravica Battalion, as far as I could remember. And I do not remember now from the top of my head but at least one of them was indicted by the state court, whether he was sentenced, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so now I'd like to understand your previous testimony where you said there was at least one -- excuse me, at least one VRS member present and participating in the killings at Kravica. Would that one member that you're talking about be the individual that's identified in the health logs from the Red Berets or this other individual that you've just now identified?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at that time when I was talking about it, I referred to the member of the Red Berets. I base it also from my experience, from my interview we conducted with the Commander of the Red Berets at that time, and it was very visible that he wanted let's say to get rid of this -- this person, you know, from his jurisdiction, let's say, at this time. He said during his interview that this person was not -- not very well subordinated soldier and he went to Kravica on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well that's a -- what I'd like to ask you about. Would you agree with me that for purposes of your investigative work, that army soldiers rarely operate individually and generally operate in units or groups while performing army duties?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So then you cannot exclude the possibility that this soldier at Kravica was indeed there for personal rather than official reasons.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exclude it because we have no proof that other members of the Red Berets were present in Kravica at that time, at least we have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in relation to this incident at Kravica warehouse, is it correct and did your investigation reveal that prior to the killings taking place, there was an attempt by at least one detainee to overpower the guards present and take the weapon of one of the guards present?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, our investigation revealed that this incident with -- related to one guard who was killed by detainee, it happened. But when it happened, this is still open question for me, in fact, whether it happened because before that there was another killings took place and whether this incident, this particular incident kind of sparked, you know, just the following events it's just the killings of entire people, you know, which were kept in Kravica warehouse. But having looked at the Kravica warehouse itself, we know it -- has been confirmed by belief that the people were kept and locked in the western part of Kravica warehouse. We have two survivors, Your Honours, we have survivor from the western part of Kravica warehouse and from eastern part of Kravica warehouse. On the Petrovic video that broadcasted or the redacted -- let's say portion from Kravica we see the bus in front of Kravica warehouse and the pile of the bodies outside the bus. We are convinced --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, what you're doing at this moment, you are giving a lot of context which, as I understand, is tending to demonstrate that what the Defence suggests must be wrong and goes far beyond what the question is. Because in the first two lines you have answered the question already. Therefore, let's proceed and try to carefully consider that you're here as a witness to answer the questions and not to defend a case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, sir, I'd like to ask you about something you just testified about. You said at temporary transcript page 59, and I will paraphrase, but you said that -- it still -- that when this incident relating to one guard who was killed by the detainee, when it happened is still an open question for you, and then you on to say, this particular incident kind of sparked, you know, just the following events being the killing of the entire people. Which particular incident may have sparked the killing of the entire people? Are we talking again about the incident where the guard was overpowered and his gun was taken? Are we talking about that still being an open issue?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I am talking about the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you recall, sir, that at one point in the video, and that would I guess be the Petrovic video which has the numbers P1538, P1541, and P1542 at the moment, do you recall that at one point in the video that as Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic are travelling and talking about the locations that they're passing that a call comes in through the radio that -- that they should come because something has happened. Do you recall that segment of the video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall conversation through the radio handset or car radio, but there is no information that something had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. With the assistance of the OTP I would like to now play that video in Sanction, and I believe the time reference I have is for P1538 which was 65 ter number 22422, and the segment at issue is from 17 minutes and 25 seconds to 17 minutes and 55 seconds approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can stop. And I note that the subtitles appear to be a little bit behind the actual audio, but recorded is an NMG on Motorola saying, "Come over, there's something."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection, sir, that in fact there was a message received over the radio to come over, there's something?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, there was such message but I'm not sure if it was directed to Mr. Borovcanin at that time because we see after this segment of the video that Mr. Borovcanin is still in the area of Sandici. It lasted at least few minutes. He didn't rush to wherever location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And did you perform any investigation to determine if in fact this was linked to anything that was going on in the area?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you ask whether we did ask Mr. Borovcanin during our interview with him what does it mean, yeah, we did. We did. But what was his answer, I do not remember from the top of my head now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough. Now, I want to move to a different topic but stay with the same part of the video. I see now we are stopped at 17 minutes and 43 seconds. If we could continue playing from this point to -- well, the entire segment is 21 minutes and 40 seconds, then I'll have some questions about what we see here, sir. So again with the assistance of Ms. Stewart and the Sanction system, if we could play it up until 21:40 on this video which is again P1538, the Petrovic raw original video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can stop here and we've stopped at 19 minutes and 12.7 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you agree with me that at this point in the video the gentleman that gave the figure of surrendered or captured persons essentially also said that that number was exaggerated?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to revisit some of your testimony from the first day when I believe the same segment was shown although the remainder of it -- but for now I'd like to focus on this section. And that's at transcript page 11.593, beginning at line 1, and I will read for you the selection: "Q. Now he, he makes a reference to them having 3.000, that 3.000 to 4.000 have surrendered. In terms of that figure, and your investigation, does that figure sound about right? "A. Yes. "Q. During your investigation, review the statements of the witnesses, and -- "A. Yeah, I believe that the figure is quite right. At this time of day, 13th of July afternoon, that they may have about few thousand of people." And that ends at line 7 of page 11.593. And the question I have for you, sir, is what statements in evidence are you referring to in your answer?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honours, I am referring to the statements of few survivors who were transported to Bratunac. They were kept in Bratunac Vuk Karadzic school and then -- and also some people were kept at the stadium and old school in Bratunac. I am referring, Your Honour, also -- we have aerial images of -- from this period from 13 July 1995. On these aerial images, aerial images of Sandici meadow, we have aerial images of Nova Kasaba soccer field. For example, on Nova Kasaba soccer field we see or calculate that at least about few hundred people kept at Nova Kasaba field. And as I said, we interviewed quite many people, not only the survivors but also the soldiers and MUP members of units who participated in this operation. But I am not referring -- I didn't want to say that this 3.000 and 4.000 were actually surrendered to this person or person, no. I was referring to general situation on the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I wanted to ask you a follow-up question, but first I have to correct with you, you say you had aerial images from the period of is it 15 July? Because we're talking about 13 July. The transcript reflects 15 July, I don't recall if you said 15 or 13 to be honest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise for my pronunciations but it is 13 July, one three.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, so far you've told us about a couple hundred people on a pitch on a soccer field. How do you get from that to 4.000? Or is this the extent of the information that you have that leads you to believe that this individual, his figure is accurate even though he's said it's not, it's exaggerated?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as far as I remember, these aerial images from the 13 July 1995, one three, July 1995, about noon -- about 2.00, if I could remember, but when Mr. Petrovic is in Sandici meadow there is already about 5.00, three hours later. We have few hundred, about 1.000 people in Nova Kasaba, let's say. We have few hundred in Sandici meadow. We know also that in mean time lot of people were transported from Nova Kasaba and from Sandici meadow to Bratunac and also to Kravica warehouse. The total number, I'm not referring even to the people, you know, just who were kept, for example, in -- at the stadium in Bratunac because unfortunately we don't have such information -- detailed information. We know that the people were kept there, there were many of them, but how many of them we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that for me, sir. Now earlier today at temporary transcript page 6 you were shown a portion of the video, I believe, later on in this same video where you talked of machine-gun fire and explosions being heard in the background while the filming was going on in Sandici. Would you agree with me that during this time, the 13th of July, 1995, that there was also shooting and fighting going on in the surrounding areas of the forest between the Bosnian Muslim column and the Serb forces which could also be the source of the sound we heard in the video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact there was a fighting but mostly the fighting was concentrated during the morning hours, you know, just a few Muslims tried to the road in the area -- yeah. That one leading from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje and then from Konjevic Polje to Milici. But we don't have any indication that fighting occurred, heavy fighting occurred in this area on the afternoon 13 July 1995, especially in Sandici area, but we have also in other statements, I believe testimony as well, one of the MUP members who -- who is referring to -- in his statement, he's referring to the shooting and explosions in Kravica warehouse. I connected all this information together.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay now. Let me see if I can understand your answer here. At lines 10 through 11, you say: "But we don't have any indication that fighting occurred, heavy fighting occurred in this area on the afternoon 13 July 1995." The question I have for you, sir, is: Are you talking about any fighting or heavy fighting? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am talking about heavy fighting. We see the Praga along the road shooting on the hills to the people who are passing through the hills, but I don't see any reverse shooting from another side toward the Serb soldiers, and we have no information that any fighting occurred in the vicinity of Sandici meadow. At this time of day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about there being any fighting at 13 July, are you saying that there was no fighting, no incoming fire from Bosnian Muslim side on 13 July? Is that your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did -- no, I didn't say that there was no fighting. Definitely there was fighting as well but not in the vicinity of Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you are not the counsel that examined the witness. It's usual that if you intervene in a witness examination, that it's done by counsel who has examined that witness. I don't know what you want to tell us, but I just bring this to your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and I understand and I try to do that as infrequently as possible. We're in an unusual situation as I have just been in another courtroom with a witness that has just provided some information that I would -- on this topic that I would like to be able to give to the Defence, because I think it's important for them to have it and I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if you give it to the Defence, that does not necessarily mean that it should be brought to the attention of the Chamber already at this moment. There is -- we have a bit of a rule that if there's late disclosure that the Chamber should be informed about that and apparently it is a disclosure issue, yes, and that rule says that if disclosure is late - not to say that any party can be blamed for it being late, but it may have arrived late - that the Chamber should be informed about it immediately, which I find a rule which is perhaps a bit questionable because if it is incriminating information, then I think it would not be appropriate to bring it immediately to the attention of the Chamber but then to bring it to the attention of the other party, in this case the Defence first. I suggest the following. Let's take an early break and disclose whatever there is that's there to be disclosed. So I do understand that you are acting as the responsible officer of the Prosecution with disclosure obligations rather than a counsel who deals with a witness examination at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break and resume at 1.30 unless the disclosure is so voluminous that you need more time, Mr. McCloskey, then the Chamber will basically wait until disclosure issues have been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could I just tell you -- I don't need to give you the information but it's a very unusual situation. I don't think it's necessarily late disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. I'm just -- we take a break now and if there's any reason to bring something to the attention of the Chamber, it can be done after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. I'm looking at you, Mr. McCloskey, and of course the Chamber becomes more and more curious what happened, but I don't know whether the parties consider it relevant to bring it to the Chamber's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would like to, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is there any objection to that before we begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's not and I can put on the record that I don't think there's any late disclosure as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So since Mr. Ivetic agrees that it should be brought to our attention, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I was just cross-examining Mr. Borovcanin who had just talked about this very issue that he was being cross-examined on, the potential gunfire in the area, and I wasn't sure they'd been watching. It turned out they had been and they had all the information so it's no problem. But I wanted to get it to him as soon as possible because he was in the middle of his cross-examination on that very point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's appropriately dealt with. It's still is late disclosure not because you were too late but it came very late which I think under the Tribunal Rules is still late disclosure. That means not before the start of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we left off talking about the 13th of July 1995 and the issue of fighting in the area. I'd like to ask you about two things. Before I get to the matter that I discussed with Mr. McCloskey, I would like to ask you of something else that I know of independently. Did your investigation reveal and demonstrate that in the morning hours of 13 July sometime approximately between 4.00 and 5.00 in the morning precisely in this area, about 500 metres from the Sandici meadows towards Konjevic Polje, that in fact armed Bosnian Muslim fighters attacked Serb forces and indeed inflicted casualties, two wounded policemen and one killed policeman in the course of this combat initiated by the Bosnian Muslim fighters precisely on the morning of 13 July 1995, 500 metres away from these Sandici meadows, did your investigation reveal that, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Our investigation confirmed that incident took place in the early morning hours of the 13th of July, 1995, but it wasn't even 500 metres from Sandici meadows, even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And now, in the Petrovic video there is -- pardon me, in the Studio B video which is P1540, I believe that there's also gunfire being heard there as the vehicle is passing the Kravica warehouse; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it's been brought to my attention that a witness in the Karadzic case, Mr. Borovcanin himself, testified yesterday that that gunfire he believed was the result of ongoing combat in the hills. Now, I'm not too concerned about Mr. Borovcanin. He's not here to testify on this matter. I want to ask you about your -- your investigative work. Can you either confirm or deny that assertion that there was gunfire going on as a result of ongoing combat in the hills even at that time as the vehicle was passing, the vehicle where Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic was passing the Kravica warehouse on the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm, either confirm or deny any fighting happened in this area when the vehicle was passing Kravica warehouse, but definitely it wasn't heavy fighting. At least I have not any information that it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, do you have any information as the result of your investigation and your many years working on this matter, do you have any material that would tend to indicate that there was heavy fighting and in fact heavy casualties resulting from the fighting in the days leading up to this time period, that is the days preceding 13 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the previous question I was referring to this time of day but yes, yes, definitely in this area, was heavy fighting also conducted by the column and VRS units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Now I'd like to look at another portion of this same video and that would be P1538 again for the record. And this is a part that is not -- I should say that was not dealt with in detail in your road booklet which is P1539 but I think it is relevant and it has been introduced now as part of the video: Do you recall later on this film there's a segment I believe from the 14th of July, 1995, when there is some footage and some interviews taken of returning Serb refugees returning to their ransacked apartments in Srebrenica town itself?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall this part of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again with the assistance of the Prosecution and the use of the Sanction system, I would like to show a segment of this video which is again P1538. And this will be the section from 30 minutes and 24 seconds to 34 minutes and 12 seconds, and I see now that we have it. And, sir, I'd ask that you follow along and then I'll have some questions about this after we view this clip, so we can be -- start it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Stop there, please. And for the record we stopped at 34 minutes and 11.3 seconds of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to take this chronologically, sir. At the beginning, first we had the one woman that's now visible on the screen in the blue shirt talking about killings that had occurred in the years prior when her husband was taken away and their children were killed by the Srebrenica defenders, the Muslim side. And this individual is talking about 23 members of his family having been killed and slaughtered. I want to ask you, did your investigative work into this area involve verifying or investigating any of these matters that were raised by these individuals interviewed on this video that we just reviewed?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was a member of the team investigating the events following the fall of or the liberation of Srebrenica. The crimes committed by the Serbs forces on the Muslim population. I was a member of this team. My colleagues, my investigative colleagues who used to work for another team, we called that at that time team 9, they investigated the crimes committed by the Muslim forces on the Serb population in this area. But we were not involved in this investigation. We are aware that these crimes happened, occurred, but we are not involved in this investigation. I mean me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And now I'd like to talk about the individual that we saw who is now visible just on the right to the screen that was interviewing by the name of Ratomir Marjanovic. Would you agree with me that although he was still in his army uniform when giving the interview, he appears to be engaging in personal tasks relating to his damaged property in Srebrenica rather than carrying out any official army function pursuant to any army orders at the time that he was being filmed?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we were to focus on what he was telling the interviewer here, that he had spent 14 days and 14 nights at his position prior to coming there, did that accord with your investigation that in fact the action in that area was so intense that Serb soldiers might have to be alert and at their positions at the front lines for up to two weeks straight before getting leave?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall from which this battalion this Marjanovic belonged to, but we know that Srebrenica operation or VRS operation started around 6th of July, 1995. We can easily calculate it. Take about eight days, five days, let's say, to the fall of Srebrenica. Of -- if -- his unit, I do not recall right now, you know, from the top of my head, you know, which unit he belonged to, but I can easily check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on the remainder of what he discussed and I think for our purposes it's probably easier to follow the transcript of the video than to replay the portions of the video with subtitles, so I'd like to call up now the transcripts of this video which is again P1538 in e-court. And in the English, it will be page 19 and in the Serbian it will be page 21 of the transcript. And, sir, if you could follow along with me while we wait for the Serbian version. The part that I'd like to focus on begins at just under the halfway point of the page and begins, "It took three to four days." And in the B/C/S, it is the approximately the fifth line from the bottom of the B/C/S transcript, and I will read from the English, sir, so that we can have exactly the parts that I'm talking about. I begin, so: "Ratko Marjanovic: It took three to four days, the driving out. "ZPP: And how long have you been on the positions? "Ratko Marjanovic: 14 days and 14 nights non--stop. "ZPP: In which direction did you chase them? "Ratko Marjanovic: In the direction of the positions in Kvarac, then Kozarici, Vidikovac, Bojna and Zanik, Solucusa, and so on." Now, sir, looking at the geographic locations that this person has identified, does that perhaps refresh your recollection as to what armed formation this gentleman would have been a member of engaged in combat with the Bosnian Muslim forces during the time period specified?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he could be the member of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, but I am not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough, sir. That's fair enough. I'd like to continue and I have some more questions. So we -- to continue where we left off which is the approximately third line from the bottom in English and then we'll go on to the next page when we get there. It goes as follows: "ZPP: Was it difficult? "Ratko Marjanovic: Yes, it was difficult. It was difficult and exhausting. "ZPP. I bet you killed a lot of their soldiers. "Ratko Marjanovic: Well yes, we did." And I'd like to end there for a moment and ask you this question: Sir, did you run across during your investigations that as a result of the heavy fighting and combat between the Serb forces and the armed Bosnian Muslim column in the days leading up to the 14th of July, 1995, that there were in fact many Bosnian Muslim soldiers or fighters killed in this combat during this time period?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the course of our investigation we established that some Muslims were killed during the time when the column tried to get to free territory. It was since 11 up to 16 July 1995. But as you -- may I, Your Honour? This is 14 July 1995, we see this member in Srebrenica. I know during the action of Srebrenica, there was not much in fact casualties from both sides, you know, just from Muslim side and if -- from the Serbian side, but later on, only during the trip that column took into the free territory, there was fighting and there was some casualties. How many, we don't know. Later on, we collected some information from the surface remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you're talking now about Srebrenica. Am I correct that this gentleman is talking about fighting that was going on in these locations leading up to that time period and were there casualties from fighting going on in Kamenica and these locations if not Srebrenica town itself?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, but this location as far as I remember from the map, because there are small hamlets if -- in fact, they are not far from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you say that your investigation did reveal that there were casualties but you don't know how many. I understand that you can't give a specific figure, but did your investigations reveal that in fact up to perhaps several thousand casualties may have resulted from the combat that was going on in the surrounding hamlets and the forests in the days from the 11th July through 16th July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely. We cannot talk about thousand casualties, you know, just during these combat operations, just the people killed during the combat. No way. It could be hundreds but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So if you have no idea, then how can you say it can't be a thousand, sir? What's the basis of your very firm affirmation that it can't be a thousand. Could you give me the evidence for that, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I can -- I will try to explain you, Your Honours. This -- the path which was taken by column to reach the free territory, it was to the hills. Most of this area was heavy mined, in fact. I do not believe and we have no indication that after the combat was over, after 16, 17 July, 1995, any organisation, whatever, whether it was -- there was the MUP units or whether it was municipality, whatever, restoration units, local units, they collected any bodies in this area because it would be too much dangerous, you know, just to go to this area to collect the bodies, you know. They left the bodies over there. After that, after some time later on, I know that it took some time after the war, in fact, you know, just the bodies were collected by -- by the commission of the missing persons. I cannot give you the figure, you know, just exactly how many but I think about few hundred along this path which was used by the column. I believe they were casualties of the combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the individuals whose bodies may not have been picked up as you say, would those not be casualties? Would those not be people that would be missing but who died under circumstances that are not what we're here for today?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies which were not picked up, you know, that they were casualties but they were casualties of the combat operation, I don't believe that they were casualties of mass executions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in relation to the -- we've been talking about the area near Srebrenica, is it also correct that during this time period, there was also some fighting going on on the territory of Zvornik municipality where a Bosnian Muslim attack occurred such that there would also be Bosnian Muslim combat fatalities or casualties on that territory. Do you have information about that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we are aware that there was a heavy fighting in the Zvornik area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And with relation to these bodies that would have been the result of combat casualties both on the Zvornik municipality and on the Srebrenica or Bratunac municipal area, would it not have been -- would it not have been standard procedure for those bodies to have been recovered and buried in joint graves or communal graves according to your understanding of the existing procedures that are applicable during a time of war as to asanacija or sanitation of the terrain or do you not know about that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely the bodies were recovered later on and put in the graves, but we are talking about 30 different graves. We are not talking about the mass graves where we found the victims of mass executions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I would point to you that RM316 has given testimony in this courtroom in that same chair that in fact we are talking about some of the same bodies. Do you have any investigation that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you'd like to have a source?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, for the witness, I'm not sure he knows who RM316 is. And if there is a source for that, that would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think we to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the witness should know, my recollection doesn't serve me well enough to know whether it is public knowledge, but if you have a source, Mr. Ivetic, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that was a protected witness and I believe that we would have to then go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you first give us a --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 23 May 2013, the same witness who talked about in the Bratunac log book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I mean page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to do that, Your Honours. My LiveNote doesn't co-operate sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I believe the witness Mr. Ivetic is referring to is RM306 and not RM316.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then for the time being, you may proceed. We'll try to find the source.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I think the witness should know who he's being referred to, whose evidence he's being referred to at the very least.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would be more than happy to if we do it in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would have to move into private session, and again I cannot say at this moment whether that is something the witness should know but let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, it's my understanding that there was also some heavy fighting going on the 12th of July, 1995, between the armed Bosnian Muslim faction and the Serb forces. Are you familiar with that, sir? If I can perhaps direct you, I believe it's Ravne Buljim was the location where that -- Ravne Buljim was the location where that fighting would have occurred on that date. Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was on the part of the column and the people were passing through this area, Ravne Buljim, and there was a fighting, heavy fighting, yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon your investigation, were there also heavy casualties as a result of that heaving fighting on the 12th of July, 1995, at Ravne Buljim?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some casualties, quite many, but how many, definitely not hundreds.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now as to those casualties quite many, what happened to those bodies? Did they also get put into graves? Are they still there? What did your investigation reveal?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are talking about mass graves containing the bodies from the mass executions, I don't think that these bodies were put in these graves, but I think they were collected later on after the war -- after the war was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have you found any evidence that these bodies were buried elsewhere apart from those mass graves?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me not but I think I believe my colleague who probably will testify in this case as well in relation to the mass graves and the victims, he may tell more about how many bodies were found where and what kind of the bodies, but I do not recall enough from the top of my head. I should refer to some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't have in front of me, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So as you sit here, you are unable to give us concrete evidence for the testimony that you gave that these bodies were not buried in the mass graves together with those that were part of the executions?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could return very briefly to what Mr. Marjanovic was saying and now we're still on the same page in both versions on this e-court. If you could follow along with me, sir, we left off where Ratko Marjanovic was saying as follows: "Well, we aren't going to do anything because all that is left -- and this needs to be smothered, all the others who stayed because we don't trust them anymore. We'll never trust them again. They killed and slaughtered 23 people in my family. "ZPP: 25? "Ratko Marjanovic: 23. Do you want to know my name? Soldier Ratomir Marjanovic. Thank you." Did your investigation into the events reveal that in fact there were a lot of people in the area who, like this individual, would be able to express great distrust and have these hard feelings against those that wronged them that killed -- to the Bosnian Muslims from Srebrenica that would have killed and slaughtered members of their family in the intervening years prior to the fall of Srebrenica. Did your investigation reveal that such sentiments were very common among the local population both civilian and otherwise of the areas around and in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. The war lasted there since 1992 up to 1995. Both sides committed crimes, also the Muslim side and the Serbian side. I'm not surprised that the Serbian population was in such mood, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that it would be entirely possible and even plausible for individuals, be they army, police, or civilian to leave from their official duties as a result of what their personal family has suffered and to entirely, for personal insecurities and sufferings extract revenge upon detained Bosnian Muslims even while still wearing their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it's not for the first time that you ask a witness whether he agrees with and then follows a full story of all kind of events where if I were a witness, even at the end I would not know what was contained in that story to which I'm supposed to say yes or no. I think it would be wiser to split it up in smaller portions. That would assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now for this part, Mr. Blaszczyk, you are reading so you have perhaps had the time to reread the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understood -- Your Honours, I understood Defence counsel that he want to say that all the killings was done by the local population who were let's say upset by -- by the activity of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the crimes committed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. What he's asking you as a matter of fact not for facts but about your personal judgement. Apart from that is what we -- but he asked you whether you consider it possible or even plausible that this was the case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's possible that some individuals took part in the killings, the private one, individuals, but these prisoners were in the custody of the army of Republika Srpska and in the custody of Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you consider it still possible for those -- I do understand your answer that you don't find it plausible for that category. You still consider it possible because then you have answered the questions put to you by Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that some individuals took the part, you know, in the pedantry from the army and police in few executions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in reference to Kravica you said there was one member of the army. Don't you think that that would potentially be more plausible of an explanation for that incident, that this individual was there for personal reasons rather than for any official capacity?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that this member of this army was there in official capacity as sent by his commander over there. We know that he was there and possibly that whatever happened over there, he did on his own. But, Your Honour, we have another document. I think this document is from the Bratunac Brigade. This document is related to this particular individual, to the Red Beret member, when there is description how he was wounded. I think in this document, there is information that he was wounded during the escorting the prisoners to Kravica warehouse. This is official military document, and I believe this document is showing us that he was in somehow in capacity of official duty in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my understanding, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm looking at the clock. I need two minutes with the parties further.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have one question left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the last question --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then put it to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, having reviewed the Petrovic film, all versions, I presume, multiple times, can you confirm for me that General Mladic does not appear anywhere on any versions of the films for Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Ms. Hasan, how much time would you need if any for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In fact, I don't think I will need any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't need any time. Since the Chamber also has no further questions for you, Mr. Blaszczyk, I'd like to thank you for coming to this courtroom and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench and you are excused. You don't have to close your eyes for e-mails any further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter I would like to briefly deal with is the e-mail which was raised with the witness. The Chamber has been copied on a message sent by Mr. Groome in which the matter is presented as Mr. Blaszczyk being inadvertently copied on an e-mail, that's how it was presented to in that e-mail. Now, in the questions Mr. Ivetic put to the witness, he gives a rather different picture where he said that after the witness had been instructed not to have any contact about his testimony, that you received an e-mail from a fellow Prosecution investigator giving precisely the substance of the meaning of the times in this log book which you were advised to disregard by the Office of the Prosecutor. Now, it's not entirely clear to me at this moment now what was in that e-mail? Did it say disregard it? Then it is not an inadvertent copying of information to the witness. Therefore -- and as the parties may understand that intervening with the testimony of a witness, if it is intentionally, may be a very serious matter. Now, therefore, could the parties in one or two words tell us what it now was? Was any instruction given to the witness or was there any direction given to the witness or was it really an inadvertent copying of e-mails that were sent to others?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think I can very quickly say I think it was inadvertent and that's the information that was given to me. I was advised immediately of it and that the instruction was given as a preventative measure to -- for him not to read the e-mail, but as we heard now, which was the part of the story that was missing, he actually had read the e-mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which you advised to disregard, therefore means that is the follow-up. You see you do it in one sentence. You say you received a e-mail from a fellow Prosecution investigator giving precisely the substance of the meaning of the times in this log book which you were advised to disregard by the Office of the Prosecutor. Now that is ambiguous language. I do understand that you're referring to a second e-mail in which the witness was advised to disregard what he read in the first one. Is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: According to the witness's testimony, a phone call, not a second e-mail, Your Honour, and again I was surprised that he had not brought it up. And earlier today, he actually started testifying about this and I would have expected a witness to say, in all due candor, that I did have this situation come up and I read the e-mail but I know this information otherwise, and that's why I went into that area of questioning because today he testified about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And didn't bring it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what I ask you at this very moment but -- are the parties willing to provide a copy of the first e-mail to the Chamber so that we at least can form an opinion about how serious the situation is? Apart from --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could suggest the information report. I presume Mr. McCloskey has that. I have no objection to that being shown and that's what I was relying upon. I think that [Overlapping Speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not evidence in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's merely to form an opinion about whether something serious came to us today or whether it was just negligence which should have perhaps been avoided but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've got these which I think you should have and I can try to tell you my recollection of it. I would probably -- well, negligence may be better a term now that I -- what happened was the issue came up with whether the log was -- admittance time or not during one of the witnesses, so in proofing Mr. Blaszczyk, we asked him, do you know, is it admittance time or time of wounding, and he said he thought it was admittance time. So he sent -- that's the proofing note that we sent. This was of course before he testified. Then we also asked someone from the field office to go to the health centre and ask the source and it was at -- my recollection is that we got an e-mail from the field office people giving us the answer to the question. That was sent to a few people including Ms. Gallagher and Ms. Gallagher copied Mr. Blaszczyk on it which is I believe while he was on the witness stand, and I saw that he was copied on that. And so I called him up immediately and said disregard that e-mail because we knew it was an interesting question. The Court had questions. The Defence had questions. And that's probably why Mr. Blaszczyk didn't deal with the topic when he was testifying about it. And we spoke to Ms. Gallagher and said please, do not communicate with people that are on the witness stand, especially about things that might be of a topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To start with, the Chamber would like to receive a copy of the relevant e-mail and that of course is not evidence in this case what is said, if you [Overlapping speakers] provide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely. I think that would help clear things up, and I think I have all of them right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you would then give them to the usher then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. That's fine. I would support that procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're fully informed about the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And I believe that Mr. McCloskey has accurately recited this incident as far as my knowledge of it is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It's 20 minutes past 2.00. I don't know how much time it takes that document to reach the 7 metres to us but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Would you like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would like to give it later today. I mean, we can leave with it not having it received until 4.00 or 5.00 or Monday morning. We just want to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely. And would you like the proofing note as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not specifically interested in it, but if you think it that it would clarify if the parties have any strong feelings about it, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have no problem with that being provided as well. I leave it in Mr. McCloskey's discretion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just one last, the issue related on the other issue related to Mr. Borovcanin, I learned that during the redirect examination a couple of hours ago while I was leading that examination. It wasn't yesterday. So I think the answer is try to stay in only one courtroom during one day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Belocation [Realtime transcript read in error "relocation."] Is not an easy thing even for professionals. If that is a -- it says "relocation" but I said belocation, I don't think whether it's an existing word in English, but being at two places at the same time. That's what I want to refer to. We will receive that document through the appropriate channels. Ms. Hasan, any?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I just simply wanted to raise that there is one document that was MFI'd. We can deal with it on Monday morning -- [Overlapping speakers] to the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do that because we are already -- I have already asked too much from interpreters and transcribers and all of those assisting us. Therefore at the end of this week, I thank all those for always having so much patience with us and we adjourn for the day and we'll resume Monday, the 10th of June, at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom I. ---Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.23 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, June 10th, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.
